newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Interstar prices A$300 mln of mortgage backed debt.
newsitem.headline: Interstar prices A$300 mln of mortgage backed debt.

text.p: Australia's Interstar Securities Pty Ltd priced on Monday the three tranche A$300 million mortgaged back securities issued under the new Interstar RD25 Master trust programme.

The A$190 million in Class A2 certificates were priced at 19 points over the 90 day bank bill swap rate (BBSW), the A$80 million in Class A3 certificates were priced at 24 points over BBSW and the A$30 million of Class B certificates were issued at 35 points over BBSW.

The Class A2 certificates had an average maturity of just under three years, the Class A3 securities had an average maturity of four-and-a-half years, while the Class B securities had a five year average life, said Simon Robinson of co-lead manager Bankers Trust Australia.
The other co-lead manager was SBC Warburg Australia, while J.B. Were Capital Markets acted in the capacity of programme adviser.
The certificates were sold to investors at par, and settlement is July 2.

Of the three tranches, the Class A certificates rank pari passu, while Class B are subordinated to all Class A certificates. The Class A certificates are rated AAA by Standard & Poor's and the Class B AA minus.
"I think we're very happy with it, it's the first time Interstar has come to the market," Robinson said. Previous issues were privately placed through institutional investors.

Interstar is one of Australia's largest independent mortgage lenders and in a statement issued by Bankers Trust when the issue was announced on June 20 it said that it is believed to be one of Australia's oldest mortgage orignators and securitisors.

Pricing was a few points higher than previous issues of similar stock, some of which was due to the fact that it was Interstar's first issue to the market but also due to the increase in mortgage-backed securities, Robinson said.
"It's a marginal increase and there's been a little bit of price resistance given the amount of supply at the moment," he said, adding that the market remained attractive to Interstar.

"Interstar will be back to the market before the year is out." Wizard Financial, which offers discount mortgages, said earlier this month that it received some of its funds from Interstar. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
